The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that on 31.10.2022 at about 10.00 a.m. the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40/EA-6578 from his residence towards his office on Bangalore-Tumkur NH-48, near Madavara Nice Road, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk,
wherein the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051 parked the same on the road,
negligently, without following any traffic rules, endangering to human life, not showed any indicator or parking lights, at the same time, the rider of the Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281 drove the same in a very rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules, endangering to human life and lost control over his motorcycle and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle from behind.
Due to sudden impact, the petitioner lost the balance over his motorcycle and dashed against the Tanker Lorry, caused the accident.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his nose, legs and hands.

3. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Life Shine Nursing Home for first aid and then he was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, Bangalore for better treatment, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and his vehicle is also badly damaged.
4. Petitioner further stated that he is still bed ridden and under treatment and so far he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment expenses.

He has to undertake further treatment and has to incur future medical expenses also and he is suffered permanent disability, he is unable to lead normal life as earlier and he is suffered huge loss of income and has lost academic year due to this accident.
5.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years and was employee at M/s. Unibic Foods India Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and earning Rs.39,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier, lost his earning capacity and also facing great financial difficulties.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051 and also motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281.

Hence, respondent No.1 and 3 being the Insurers and respondent NO.2 and 4 being the owners of the offending vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner on the heads of pain and suffering, shock,
physical and mental agony, medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses, loss of income, loss of future earning capacity, loss of amenities, future medical expenses and permanent disability etc.,

At the same time rider of one Honda Shine Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281 rode the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and dashed the petitioner from behind.

sentences.text: 23. The respondent No.1 to 3 took contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
As per Ex.P.4 IMV report, the damages caused to the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40/EA-6578 is that the handle bar damaged, crash guard left side damaged and rear left side indicator damaged.
The damaged caused to the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051 is that the rear bumper middle portion damaged and front bumper left side damaged.

The damages caused to the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281 is that the head light mask damaged, front both side indicator damaged, front number plate damaged, handle bar damaged, rear left side indicator damaged and crash guard right side damaged.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 the complaint and Ex.P.3 the spot mahazar

, it appears that the accident took place due to negligent act of driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051 and the rider of another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281.
24.

After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R, Ex.P.2-complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P.4 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.10 and 11 are the copies of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.12 and 13 are the copies of reply to notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act,
Ex.P.14 and 15 are the copies of indemnity bonds, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of Tanker Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051 and the rider of another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U- 6281.

On perusal of entire materials on record, it appears that the Tanker Lorry was parked on the road without giving any signals, if the driver or owner of the Tanker Lorry was taken the proper precautions, then, the accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, the tanker lorry has its major involvement in the said accident.
The motorcycle Reg.No.KA- 64/U-6281 is also had some contributory negligence.
Accordingly, some contributory negligence taken on the part of the rider of motorcycle and on the major part of the driver of the offending Tanker Lorry.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that Tanker Lorry has major negligence and motorcycle has some contributed his negligence in the accident.

Accordingly,
apportion of the negligence on the part of the offending Tanker Lorry is taken at 60% and on the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-64/U-6281 is taken at 40%.
Hence, this Tribunal answers the Issue No.1 Partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificate and discharge summary issued by Prakriya Hospitals, Nagasandra, Bangalore at Ex.P.5 and P.9 and prayed to award compensation amount.
The Respondents not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:-

The doctor opined that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.

33. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

34. Liability:-
In this case respondent No.1 is the Insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Tanker Lorry Reg.No.KA-41/B-7051.
Respondent No.3 and 4 are the insurer and owner of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64/U-6281.
